sentences.text:
This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/Physical Mode).
2.
This is an application by the petitioner for grant of interim bail on the ground of illness of his mother.
3. Heard, Mr. Binod Kumar Hati, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. P. Satpathy, learned Additional Public Prosecutor in the matter and perused the record.

4. The petitioner has sought for interim bail on the ground to attend his ailing mother who is suffering from chronic arthritics with stiffness, but only disability certificate of the mother of the petitioner has been enclosed together with one prescription, which does not disclose about the mother of the petitioner suffering from arthritics.

5. In such view of the matter and after having considered the rival submissions and taking into account the averments made in the IA, which is not supported by any medical documents, this Court does not find any good ground to grant interim bail to the petitioner.
Hence, the present application for grant of interim bail to the petitioner stands rejected.

sentences.text: This is a bail application U/S.483 of BNSS by the petitioner for grant of bail in connection with Tureikela PS Case No.42 of 2023 corresponding to Special GR Case No.31 of 2023 pending in the file of learned Additional Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge under POCSO Act, Bolangir, for commission of offences punishable U/Ss.363/ 376(3)/ 376(2)(n) of IPC r/w Section 6 of POCSO Act and Sections 3(2)(v)(va) of SC & ST (PoA) Act, on the main allegation of kidnapping the victim and committing rape and aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon her by taking advantage of her caste.

8. Heard, Mr. Binod Kumar Hati, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. P. Satpathy, learned Additional Public Prosecutor in the matter and perused the record.
9. Bail is mainly sought for to the petitioner on the ground that the victim is a consenting party, but it appears from the materials placed on record that the victim is prima facie not more than 18 years.
In such view of the matter and after having considered the rival submissions and taking into consideration the nature and gravity of the offences as alleged against the petitioner vis--vis the accusations sought to be brought against him and regard being had to the statement of the victim,
this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the petitioner at this stage, when the victim is yet to be examined in the trial.
10. Hence, the bail application of the petitioner stands rejected.
11. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy of the order as per Rules.
